GERMAN — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #13
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: GERMAN
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Reading aloud, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading aloud.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading aloud.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading aloud.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading aloud.

2. When practising Listening for gist, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for gist.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening for gist.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for gist.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening for gist.

3. German for “school” is: (1 mark)
   A. Schule
   B. Buch
   C. Wasser
   D. Haus

4. When practising Guided Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Guided Reading.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Guided Reading.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Guided Reading.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Guided Reading.

5. When practising Phonological awareness, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Phonological awareness.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Phonological awareness.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Phonological awareness.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological awareness.

6. When practising Interactive speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive speaking.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Interactive speaking.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Interactive speaking.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive speaking.

7. When practising Selective Listening, Imitative speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Selective Listening, Imitative speaking.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Selective Listening, Imitative speaking.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Selective Listening, Imitative speaking.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Selective Listening, Imitative speaking.

8. “Guten Tag” means: (1 mark)
   A. Good day / hello
   B. Good night
   C. Thank you
   D. Please

9. When practising Guided reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Guided reading.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Guided reading.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Guided reading.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Guided reading.

10. When practising Oral expressions, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Oral expressions.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Oral expressions.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral expressions.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Oral expressions.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
11. In three clear sentences, explain Listening for gist and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

12. In three clear sentences, explain Phonological awareness and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

13. In three clear sentences, explain Interactive speaking and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Oral expressions and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading aloud.

2. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for gist.

3. A — Schule

4. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Guided Reading.

5. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological awareness.

6. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive speaking.

7. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Selective Listening, Imitative speaking.

8. A — Good day / hello

9. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Guided reading.

10. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral expressions.

11. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening for gist; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

12. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Phonological awareness; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Interactive speaking; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Oral expressions; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
